newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks edge up by close on cheap prices.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks edge up by close on cheap prices.

text.p: Lima stocks edged up slightly over all by the close Tuesday as local investors took advantage of cheaply-priced stocks and the market benefitted from other gains around the region, brokers said.
They predicted stability or a continued slight upward trend for Wednesday's session.

"The prices are very low and it is the right moment to take positions despite rumors that gross domestic product (GDP) figures (for November) won't be as good as expected," said Jose Luis Infante of Interlima brokerage.
In Tuesday's session, the General Index rose 0.39 percent to 1,443.8 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index gained 0.58 percent to 2,043.3 points, according to preliminary market figures.
"The market continues to recover after various falls," said Aldo Ferrini of Provalor brokerage.
Total market volume was 24.2 million soles ($9.3 million) on 1,305 trades.

Among leaders, benchmark Telefnica del Per gained 0.59 percent to 5.11 soles on 1.4 million shares, while brewery Compaa Nacional de Cerveza rose 1.52 percent to 1.34 soles on 657,169 shares, and electricity distributor Luz del Sur edged up 1.15 percent to 3.53 soles on 188,159 shares.
Losers included Southern Copper Corp, off 1.57 percent to $15.70 on 8,650 shares, and food company Consorcio de Alimentos Fabril Pacfico, which gained 0.28 percent to 3.61 soles on 9,097 shares.
